items.hi: रविवार को पिताजी बिना कहीं ख़ास जाने के इरादे के, अकेले बाहर निकल गए।
items.gu: રવિવારે પિતાજી ક્યાંય ખાસ જવાના ઇરાદા વિના, એકલા બહાર નીકળી ગયા.
items.why: The verb after ともなしに should be the same kind of action done aimlessly (前後に同じ動詞を使うことが多い) — going out matches 行く. a) staying home means he didn't go anywhere at all. c) thinking has nothing to do with going somewhere.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）わたしは彼を尊敬するようになった。
items.qr: (___) watashi wa kare o sonkei suru you ni natta.
items.en: I can't say exactly when it began, but I've come to respect him.
items.hi: न जाने कब से, मैं उसका सम्मान करने लगा।
items.gu: ખબર નહીં ક્યારથી, હું તેનો આદર કરવા લાગ્યો.
items.why: 〜ようになった describes a change over time, so the unclear element is when → いつから + ともなく. b) だれともなく means "someone unspecified", but the subject is clearly わたし. a) 何 is not a time/place/person question word, so it doesn't fit meaning B.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: さっきまであの木の枝に鳥が数羽いたが、（ ）飛んでいってしまった。
items.qr: Sakki made ano ki no eda ni tori ga suuwa ita ga, (___) tonde itte shimatta.
items.en: There were a few birds on that branch a moment ago, but they flew off to who knows where.
items.hi: अभी कुछ देर पहले उस पेड़ की डाल पर कुछ पक्षी थे, पर न जाने कहाँ उड़ गए।
items.gu: હમણાં થોડી વાર પહેલાં તે ઝાડની ડાળ પર થોડાં પક્ષી હતાં, પણ ખબર નહીં ક્યાં ઊડી ગયાં.
items.why: Flying off to somewhere needs a direction: question word + particle へ → どこへともなく (疑問詞と助詞の組み合わせ). b) lacks the particle that ties it to 飛んでいく. c) a count (何羽) isn't a time/place/person question word — and we already know there were 数羽.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 大川選手は走るのも速いしボールの扱いもうまい。（ ）サッカー選手だ。
items.qr: Ookawa senshu wa hashiru no mo hayai shi booru no atsukai mo umai. (___) sakkaa senshu da.
items.en: Okawa is a fast runner and great with the ball. He's a born footballer.
items.hi: ओकावा तेज़ दौड़ता है और गेंद पर भी उसकी अच्छी पकड़ है। वह जन्मजात फ़ुटबॉलर है।
items.gu: ઓકાવા ઝડપથી દોડે છે અને બૉલ પર પણ સારી પકડ છે. તે જન્મજાત ફૂટબૉલર છે.
items.why: The connection is 動 ます-stem + ながら: 生まれ(ます) → 生まれながら, and before a noun it takes の. a) dictionary form and c) た形 are not allowed.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 祖母は（ ）戦争中の思い出話を語った。
items.qr: Sobo wa (___) sensouchuu no omoide banashi o katatta.
items.en: My grandmother, in tears, told us her memories of the war.
items.hi: दादी ने रोते हुए युद्ध के दिनों की यादें सुनाईं।
items.gu: દાદીએ રડતાં-રડતાં યુદ્ધના દિવસોની યાદો સંભળાવી.
items.why: The blank modifies the verb 語った, so the adverbial 〜ながらに is needed — 涙ながらに is the fixed idiom meaning 泣きながら. a) 〜の would need a noun right after (涙ながらの訴え). b) 〜で is not a form of this pattern.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 久しぶりにふるさとを訪れた。（ ）古い家がわたしを迎えてくれた。
items.qr: Hisashiburi ni furusato o otozureta. (___) furui ie ga watashi o mukaete kureta.
items.en: I visited my hometown for the first time in ages. The old house, unchanged from the old days, welcomed me.
items.hi: बहुत दिनों बाद अपने गाँव गया। पुराने ज़माने जैसा वही पुराना घर मेरा स्वागत करने को खड़ा था।
items.gu: ઘણા સમય પછી મારા વતન ગયો. જૂના જમાના જેવું એ જ જૂનું ઘર મારું સ્વાગત કરવા ઊભું હતું.
items.why: The blank modifies the noun 古い家, so 〜ながらの. c) 〜に would modify a verb (昔ながらに作られている). b) 〜で is not used.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 立ち食いそば屋は、座らないで（ ）そばを食べる店です。
items.qr: Tachigui sobaya wa, suwaranaide (___) soba o taberu mise desu.
items.en: A standing soba bar is a shop where you eat soba standing up rather than sitting down.
items.hi: "तचिगुई सोबा" दुकान ऐसी जगह है जहाँ बैठे बिना खड़े होकर सोबा खाते हैं।
items.gu: "તાચિગુઈ સોબા" દુકાન એવી જગ્યા છે જ્યાં બેઠા વિના ઊભા રહીને સોબા ખવાય છે.
items.why: 〜ながらに(して) works only with a limited set of words (限られた言葉にしかつかない), and 立つ isn't one of them — so b) is out. For the state in which you do something, Japanese uses the て形: 立って食べる. c) 立ちながら (the "simultaneous action" ながら) is unnatural because 立つ is a change-of-posture verb.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 今度の議長はどうも甘い言い方をするきらいがあると、みんなに（ ）。
items.qr: Kondo no gichou wa doumo amai iikata o suru kirai ga aru to, minna ni (___).
items.en: The new chair is being criticised by everyone for having a tendency to put things too softly.
items.hi: नए अध्यक्ष की बहुत नरमी से बात कहने की आदत है, इसलिए सब उनकी आलोचना कर रहे हैं।
items.gu: નવા અધ્યક્ષની બહુ નરમાશથી વાત કહેવાની ટેવ છે, એટલે બધા તેમની ટીકા કરી રહ્યા છે.
items.why: きらいがある is criticism (主に人を批判して言う), so what people do about it is 批判する. b) praise and c) being welcomed contradict the negative judgment.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: うちの子は（ ）きらいがある。
items.qr: Uchi no ko wa (___) kirai ga aru.
items.en: My child has a tendency to exaggerate things.
items.hi: मेरे बच्चे की बातों को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर कहने की आदत है।
items.gu: મારા બાળકને વાતોને વધારી-ચઢાવીને કહેવાની ટેવ છે.
items.why: Only a bad tendency (良くない傾向) can come before きらいがある. Exaggerating is a fault; a) loving animals and b) tidying up are good habits.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: （ ）頭で考えるだけで行動に移さないきらいがある。
items.qr: (___) atama de kangaeru dake de koudou ni utsusanai kirai ga aru.
items.en: My younger brother has a tendency to just think things over in his head and never act on them.
items.hi: मेरे छोटे भाई की आदत है कि वह बस दिमाग़ में सोचता रहता है, अमल नहीं करता।
items.gu: મારા નાના ભાઈની ટેવ છે કે તે બસ મનમાં વિચારતો રહે છે, અમલ કરતો નથી.
items.why: きらいがある criticises another person and is normally not used about oneself (ふつう話者自身のことには使わない) → 弟. a) is first person. c) a place/country isn't the "person" whose habit is being criticised, and 日本では doesn't give the sentence a subject who "thinks only in his head".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: うちの夫は（ ）きらいがある。
items.qr: Uchi no otto wa (___) kirai ga aru.
items.en: My husband has a tendency to take up too many hobbies.
items.hi: मेरे पति की ज़रूरत से ज़्यादा शौक़ पाल लेने की आदत है।
items.gu: મારા પતિને જરૂર કરતાં વધારે શોખ પાળી લેવાની ટેવ છે.

opts.en: spreads himself too thin with hobbies
opts.hi: बहुत ज़्यादा शौक़ फैला लेते हैं
opts.gu: બહુ વધારે શોખ ફેલાવી દે છે

items.why: きらいがある describes a tendency/habit (傾向・くせ) that the speaker sees as a bit bad. 〜すぎる shows a habitual excess. a) and b) are just facts/states about how many hobbies he has, not a tendency in his behaviour.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 彼女は、周りを（ ）の行動力の持ち主だ。
items.qr: Kanojo wa, mawari o (___) no koudouryoku no mochinushi da.
items.en: She has a drive so powerful it practically overwhelms everyone around her.
items.hi: उसमें ऐसी कर्मठता है मानो आसपास के सबको पीछे छोड़ देगी।
items.gu: તેનામાં એવી કર્મઠતા છે જાણે આસપાસના બધાને પાછળ છોડી દેશે.
items.why: An unusual degree ("so strong it nearly overwhelms") → 〜んばかり, with the する-exception: 圧倒せんばかり. b) and c) とばかり describes an unspoken utterance shown through an action — 行動力 is a quality, not an act of "saying" anything.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 試験中ちょっと横を（ ）、カンニングと間違われた。
items.qr: Shikenchuu chotto yoko o (___), kanningu to machigawareta.
items.en: Just because I glanced sideways during the exam, I was mistaken for cheating.
items.hi: परीक्षा के दौरान बस ज़रा बगल में देख लिया, इसी वजह से मुझ पर नक़ल का शक हो गया।
items.gu: પરીક્ષા દરમિયાન બસ જરા બાજુમાં જોયું, એટલા કારણે જ મારા પર નકલનો શક થયો.
items.why: The answer is the N2 form 〜たばかりに ("just because ~, something bad happened") — not one of this lesson's points; the set mixes it in as a trap. a) 〜んばかり would mean he "almost looked", but he actually did. b) とばかり needs an unspoken utterance acted out, which doesn't fit being suspected.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: だれに（ ）「春だなあ」とつぶやいた。
items.qr: Dare ni (___) "haru da naa" to tsubuyaita.
items.en: To no one in particular, I murmured, "Ah, it's spring."
items.hi: किसी ख़ास से कहे बिना, मैंने धीरे से कहा, "वसंत आ गया।"
items.gu: કોઈને ખાસ કહ્યા વિના, મેં ધીમેથી કહ્યું, "વસંત આવી ગઈ."

opts.en: without saying it to anyone in particular

items.why: だれに言うともなく is the standard phrase "addressed to no one in particular" — meaning A of ともなく (no clear intention) with a question word. a) 言う is not one of the few words that take ながらにして. c) とばかり would mean he didn't say anything aloud, yet つぶやいた says he did.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 失敗して落ち込んでいたら、（ ）みんなに肩をたたかれた。
items.qr: Shippai shite ochikonde itara, (___) minna ni kata o tatakareta.
items.en: When I was feeling down after my failure, everyone patted me on the shoulder as if to say, "Cheer up!"
items.hi: नाकामी से मैं उदास था, तो सबने मानो कह रहे हों "हिम्मत रखो", मेरा कंधा थपथपाया।
items.gu: નિષ્ફળતાથી હું ઉદાસ હતો, તો બધાએ જાણે કહેતા હોય "હિંમત રાખ", મારો ખભો થાબડ્યો.

opts.t: 元気を出さんばかりに
元気を出したばかりに
opts.hi: बस जोश में आने की वजह से

opts.t: 元気を出せとばかりに
opts.r: genki o dase to bakari ni

items.why: The pat on the shoulder silently says "元気を出せ!" — a command-form utterance + とばかりに. a) 〜んばかり would describe the patters' own state ("almost cheering up"), which isn't the point. b) 〜たばかりに ("just because") gives a cause of something bad, which doesn't fit.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 6課 · 様子

items.q: 運動がてら（ ）。
items.qr: Undou gatera (___).
items.en: I went out walking the dog, partly for some exercise.
items.hi: थोड़ी कसरत भी हो जाए, इसलिए कुत्ते को टहलाने निकल गया।
items.gu: થોડી કસરત પણ થઈ જાય, એટલે કૂતરાને ફેરવવા નીકળી ગયો.

opts.t: 運動場まで行ってきた
opts.hi: खेल के मैदान तक हो आया

opts.en: went out to walk the dog

items.why: 〜がてら + a separate action that involves going out, which takes advantage of A. Walking the dog doubles as exercise. c) running 3 km is the exercise — nothing extra is being done. a) going to a sports ground is just the place to exercise, not a second errand.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）図書館に行った。
items.qr: (___) toshokan ni itta.
items.en: I went to the library while I was out shopping.
items.hi: ख़रीदारी करते-करते लाइब्रेरी भी हो आया।
items.gu: ખરીદી કરતાં-કરતાં લાઇબ્રેરી પણ જઈ આવ્યો.
items.why: A should be an outing (移動を含む動作) different from the main purpose. Shopping is a separate trip; the library is the add-on. b) and c) borrowing / looking for books are the reason for going to a library — there's no "taking the chance" here.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）車の展示場をのぞいた。
items.qr: (___) kuruma no tenjijou o nozoita.
items.en: While out having fun, I took a peek at a car showroom.
items.hi: घूमते-फिरते, कार शोरूम में भी झाँक आया।
items.gu: ફરતાં-હરતાં, કાર શોરૂમમાં પણ ડોકિયું કરી આવ્યો.

opts.t: いい車を見つけがてら

items.why: 遊び here means "going out for fun", an outing during which you drop in somewhere. a) 見つける is a non-volitional result, not an outing (and finding a car is what you'd do at the showroom). b) hurrying is a manner, not an activity you can piggyback on — and it contradicts casually "peeking in".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）かたがた近いうちに恩師を訪ねようと思っている。
items.qr: (___) katagata chikai uchi ni onshi o tazuneyou to omotte iru.
items.en: I'm thinking of visiting my old teacher soon, partly to tell him I've found a job.
items.hi: सोच रहा हूँ कि जल्द ही नौकरी लगने की ख़बर देने के साथ अपने गुरुजी से मिलने जाऊँ।
items.gu: વિચારું છું કે જલદી નોકરી મળ્યાના સમાચાર આપવાની સાથે મારા ગુરુજીને મળવા જાઉં.
items.why: The noun is another purpose (別の目的) for the visit — a report is a classic one. a) 訪問 is the visit itself (訪ねる), so it's redundant. b) 食事 is not a polite purpose for calling on a teacher, and doesn't fit the formal tone of かたがた.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）かたがた、お宅に伺います。
items.qr: (___) katagata, otaku ni ukagaimasu.
items.en: I'll call at your home, partly to pay my respects.
items.hi: मिलने-जुलने (अभिवादन) के इरादे से भी मैं आपके घर आऊँगा।
items.gu: મળવા-હળવા (અભિવાદન)ના ઇરાદાથી પણ હું આપને ઘરે આવીશ.
items.why: ごあいさつ is a polite purpose for a visit → ごあいさつかたがた伺う. b) a holiday is a time, not a purpose. c) おじゃま (する) means visiting someone's home — the same act as 伺う, so it can't be the "other" purpose.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 叔母が体調を崩したと聞いたので、見舞いかたがた（ ）。
items.qr: Oba ga taichou o kuzushita to kiita node, mimai katagata (___).
items.en: I heard my aunt had fallen ill, so I went to help her out and to see how she was.
items.hi: सुना कि चाची की तबीयत ख़राब है, तो हालचाल पूछने के साथ मदद करने भी चला गया।
items.gu: સાંભળ્યું કે કાકીની તબિયત બગડી છે, તો ખબર-અંતર પૂછવાની સાથે મદદ કરવા પણ ગયો.
items.why: The book's rule: after かたがた, a verb of movement (行く・訪ねる) is typical. b) 〜に行った supplies that. a) 手伝った has no movement. c) sending fruit means you didn't go — and 見舞い is a visit purpose.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 彼は（ ）のかたわらNPOの活動をしている。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) no katawara enu-pii-oo no katsudou o shite iru.
items.en: Alongside his creative work, he is active in an NPO.
items.hi: वह अपने रचनात्मक काम के साथ-साथ एक NPO (स्वयंसेवी संस्था) में भी काम करता है।
items.gu: તે પોતાના સર્જનાત્મક કામની સાથે-સાથે એક NPO (સ્વયંસેવી સંસ્થા)માં પણ કામ કરે છે.
items.why: かたわら attaches to the main occupation (本業となる仕事). Creative work (writing, art) is his profession. a) living alone is a lifestyle, not work. c) a hobby is by definition not one's main job.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 母は（ ）かたわら翻訳の仕事もしている。
items.qr: Haha wa (___) katawara hon'yaku no shigoto mo shite iru.
items.en: Besides teaching maths, my mother also does translation work.
items.hi: माँ गणित पढ़ाने के साथ-साथ अनुवाद का काम भी करती हैं।
items.gu: મા ગણિત ભણાવવાની સાથે-સાથે અનુવાદનું કામ પણ કરે છે.
items.why: Teaching maths is a profession, so translation can run "beside" it. b) cooking dinner and c) listening to music are momentary daily activities — they'd take 〜ながら (simultaneous), not かたわら.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 山中さんは市役所に勤めるかたわら（ ）。
items.qr: Yamanaka-san wa shiyakusho ni tsutomeru katawara (___).
items.en: Alongside his job at city hall, Mr. Yamanaka is also active as a singer.
items.hi: यामानाका जी नगर-निगम में नौकरी करने के साथ-साथ गायक के रूप में भी सक्रिय हैं।
items.gu: યામાનાકાજી નગરપાલિકામાં નોકરી કરવાની સાથે-સાથે ગાયક તરીકે પણ સક્રિય છે.

opts.t: 歌手としても活躍している
opts.r: kashu to shite mo katsuyaku shite iru
opts.en: is also active as a singer
opts.hi: गायक के रूप में भी सक्रिय हैं

opts.t: いつも忙しくしている
家では年を取った親の世話をしている
opts.r: ie de wa toshi o totta oya no sewa o shite iru
opts.en: looks after his elderly parents at home
opts.hi: घर पर बूढ़े माता-पिता की देखभाल करते हैं
opts.gu: ઘરે વૃદ્ધ માતા-પિતાની સંભાળ રાખે છે

items.why: After かたわら comes a social activity separate from the main job (本業とは別の社会的活動). A singing career fits. b) "being busy" is a state, not an activity. c) caring for one's parents is private family life, not a social activity.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 母は（ ）よく音楽を聞いている。
items.qr: Haha wa (___) yoku ongaku o kiite iru.
items.en: My mother often listens to music while she does the gardening.
items.hi: माँ अक्सर बाग़बानी करते हुए संगीत सुनती हैं।
items.gu: મા ઘણી વાર બાગકામ કરતાં-કરતાં સંગીત સાંભળે છે.

opts.t: 庭仕事をするかたわら

items.why: Two actions at the same moment → plain 〜ながら. b) かたわら is for a main occupation plus a separate long-term activity; gardening isn't her job and listening to music isn't a social activity. a) かたがた needs a polite purpose for a visit and a movement verb.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: 今回のことでは取引先に迷惑をかけてしまった。（ ）あいさつに行ってこよう。
items.qr: Konkai no koto de wa torihikisaki ni meiwaku o kakete shimatta. (___) aisatsu ni itte koyou.
items.en: We caused our client trouble over this matter. I'll go and pay them a visit, partly to apologise.
items.hi: इस मामले में हमने अपने ग्राहक को परेशानी में डाल दिया। माफ़ी माँगने के इरादे से भी उनसे मिल आता हूँ।
items.gu: આ મામલામાં અમે અમારા ગ્રાહકને તકલીફમાં મૂકી દીધા. માફી માગવાના ઇરાદાથી પણ તેમને મળી આવું.

opts.hi: माफ़ी माँगने के इरादे से भी

items.why: A formal business visit with a second polite purpose (apology) + a movement verb (行く) → かたがた. a) がてら is casual and needs an outing-type noun (散歩, 買い物); おわび isn't a movement activity you squeeze an errand into. b) an apology is not someone's main occupation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）神社にお参りしてきた。
items.qr: (___) jinja ni omairi shite kita.
items.en: While out cherry-blossom viewing, I stopped by a shrine to pray.
items.hi: चेरी-ब्लॉसम देखने निकला था, तो साथ में मंदिर (神社) में दर्शन भी कर आया।
items.gu: ચેરી-બ્લૉસમ જોવા નીકળ્યો હતો, તો સાથે મંદિર (神社)માં દર્શન પણ કરી આવ્યો.

opts.en: partly for (the polite purpose of) flower viewing
opts.hi: फूल देखने के (औपचारिक) इरादे से भी

items.why: 花見 is a leisurely outing (移動を含む動作) and the shrine visit is squeezed into it → がてら. b) かたがた is for polite social purposes (お礼・報告・見舞い), not a leisure outing. c) flower viewing is not an occupation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 7課 · 付随行動

items.q: （ ）ところをおじゃましました。
items.qr: (___) tokoro o ojama shimashita.
items.en: I'm sorry to have disturbed you on your day off.
items.hi: आपकी छुट्टी के दिन आपको परेशान किया, क्षमा कीजिए।
items.gu: આપની રજાના દિવસે આપને હેરાન કર્યા, માફ કરશો.
items.why: The 🔗 line says 名 だ −の + ところを, so a noun links with の: お休みのところを. a) a bare noun can't attach directly to ところ; b) な is the link for な-adjectives, and お休み is a noun.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: すぐに（ ）ところを遅くなってしまいまして、申し訳ありません。
items.qr: Sugu ni (___) tokoro o osoku natte shimaimashite, moushiwake arimasen.
items.en: I should have informed you immediately, and I'm very sorry it has been so late.
items.hi: मुझे आपको तुरंत सूचित करना चाहिए था, देर हो जाने के लिए क्षमा चाहता हूँ।
items.gu: મારે આપને તરત જાણ કરવી જોઈતી હતી, મોડું થઈ જવા બદલ માફી માગું છું.
items.why: This is the book's example ③ type, 〜べきところを: "when I ought to have done X (I didn't, and I'm sorry)". すぐに + 遅くなって only makes sense with "should have". a) お知らせするところを would mean "just when I was about to inform you" — no reason to apologise for lateness. c) お知らせした says it was already done, which contradicts 遅くなって.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: お忙しいところを（ ）。
items.qr: Oisogashii tokoro o (___).
items.en: Thank you for helping me when you were so busy.
items.hi: आप इतने व्यस्त थे, फिर भी मदद करने के लिए धन्यवाद।
items.gu: આપ આટલા વ્યસ્ત હતા, છતાં મદદ કરવા બદલ આભાર.

opts.t: 手伝ってくださってありがとうございました
何かお手伝いしましょうか

items.why: The ⚠ note: 〜ところを is a courtesy phrase for having troubled the listener, followed by an apology or thanks. b) is thanks for the trouble. a) is encouragement and c) is an offer — in neither has the speaker troubled the listener.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）事故は起こらなかったものを、本当に残念なことになってしまった。
items.qr: (___) jiko wa okoranakatta mono o, hontou ni zannen na koto ni natte shimatta.
items.en: If they had been careful the accident wouldn't have happened — it's turned out truly regrettable.
items.hi: सावधानी बरती होती तो दुर्घटना न होती, पर बहुत अफ़सोसनाक हो गया।
items.gu: સાવચેતી રાખી હોત તો અકસ્માત ન થાત, પણ ખૂબ દુઃખદ બની ગયું.
items.why: ものを attaches to a sentence that supposes something contrary to fact (事実とは異なることを仮定した文). 〜ていれば … なかった is that counterfactual. b) 〜と is a general/habitual condition, not a regretful "if only". c) the て-form states a fact ("they were careful"), which contradicts the accident happening.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 会いたいと言っているんだから会ってあげればいいものを。どうして（ ）の。
items.qr: Aitai to itte iru n da kara atte agereba ii mono o. Doushite (___) no.
items.en: He's saying he wants to see you, so you could just meet him. Why won't you?
items.hi: वह मिलना चाहता है, तो मिल लेना चाहिए था। तुम क्यों नहीं मिलते?
items.gu: તે મળવા માગે છે, તો મળી લેવું જોઈએ. તું કેમ નથી મળતો?
items.why: After 〜ものを comes the sentence describing the actual fact, which is the opposite of the "good" supposition. The supposition is "you should meet him", so the reality — and the source of the speaker's frustration — is that you don't. a) and b) agree with the supposition, so there would be nothing to complain about.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 行きたくないのなら、（ ）ものを。
items.qr: Ikitakunai no nara, (___) mono o.
items.en: If you didn't want to go, you shouldn't have gone (yet you did).
items.hi: अगर जाना नहीं चाहते थे, तो न जाते (पर तुम चले गए)।
items.gu: જો જવું નહોતું, તો ન ગયો હોત તો સારું હતું (પણ તું ગયો).

opts.t: 行かなければいけなかった
行かなければよかった

items.why: 〜ものを = "it would have been good if ~ (but it didn't happen)". Given 行きたくない, the good outcome is not going; the omitted reality is "you went". c) fits. b) "you should have gone" contradicts 行きたくないのなら. a) is an obligation, not a desirable counterfactual, so there's no regret for ものを to express.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）ものを、何も言わなければわかってもらえないよ。
items.qr: (___) mono o, nani mo iwanakereba wakatte moraenai yo.
items.en: If you talked to them they'd understand — but if you say nothing, they never will.
items.hi: बात करो तो वे समझ जाएँगे, पर कुछ नहीं कहोगे तो कोई नहीं समझेगा।
items.gu: વાત કરે તો તેઓ સમજી જાય, પણ કંઈ નહીં કહે તો કોઈ નહીં સમજે.

opts.en: even if you talk, they won't understand
opts.hi: बात करने पर भी नहीं समझेंगे

opts.t: 話せばわからなくなる
opts.en: if you talk, they'll stop understanding
opts.hi: बात करोगे तो और नहीं समझेंगे
opts.gu: વાત કરશો તો વધુ નહીં સમજે

items.why: ものを needs the "things would have gone well" supposition (順当に成立していれば良かった). Only a) gives the good outcome that the reality (saying nothing) then spoils. b) and c) describe bad outcomes even if you talk, so there's no regret and no contrast with 何も言わなければわかってもらえない.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 試験の結果は予想していた通りだとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Shiken no kekka wa yosou shite ita toori da to wa ie, (___).
items.en: The exam result may have been just what I'd expected, but it was still a shock.
items.hi: माना कि परीक्षा का नतीजा उम्मीद के मुताबिक़ ही था, फिर भी झटका तो लगा।
items.gu: માન્યું કે પરીક્ષાનું પરિણામ ધાર્યા મુજબ જ હતું, છતાં આઘાત તો લાગ્યો.

opts.t: あまりショックではなかった
opts.en: it wasn't much of a shock

opts.t: やはりショックだった

items.why: After とはいえ comes the speaker's evaluation against what the first half implies. "As expected" implies "no shock", so the contrary feeling — still a shock — fits (note やはり "even so"). a) follows naturally from 予想通り, so there's no contrast. b) is a bare fact, not an evaluation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: あの党は支持率が落ちたとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Ano tou wa shijiritsu ga ochita to wa ie, (___).
items.en: That party's approval rating may have dropped, but it's probably not yet to the point of losing power.
items.hi: माना कि उस दल का समर्थन घटा है, फिर भी अभी सत्ता छिन जाने जैसी हालत नहीं होगी।
items.gu: માન્યું કે તે પક્ષનું સમર્થન ઘટ્યું છે, છતાં હજી સત્તા છીનવાઈ જાય એવી હાલત નહીં હોય.

opts.t: まだ政権を奪われるほどではないだろう
opts.r: mada seiken o ubawareru hodo de wa nai darou
opts.en: it's probably not yet bad enough to lose power
opts.hi: अभी सत्ता छिनने लायक़ हालत नहीं होगी
opts.gu: હજી સત્તા છીનવાય એવી હાલત નહીં હોય

opts.t: 反省する態度が見られない
opts.en: it shows no sign of remorse
opts.hi: पछतावे का कोई भाव नहीं दिखता

opts.t: また新しい政策を打ち出した
opts.hi: उसने फिर एक नई नीति घोषित की
opts.gu: તેણે ફરી નવી નીતિ જાહેર કરી

items.why: a) is a judgment (〜だろう) that pushes back against "approval fell" → "still not that bad". b) is a criticism, but it doesn't run against the first half (falling support and no remorse point the same way). c) is just a reported event, not the speaker's evaluation.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 有給休暇があるとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Yuukyuu kyuuka ga aru to wa ie, (___).
items.en: We may have paid leave, but actually taking time off is never easy.
items.hi: माना कि सवेतन छुट्टी मिलती है, फिर भी छुट्टी लेना आसान नहीं होता।
items.gu: માન્યું કે પગારવાળી રજા મળે છે, છતાં રજા લેવી સહેલી હોતી નથી.

opts.t: 昨年は休みを取らなかった
opts.en: I didn't take any leave last year
opts.hi: पिछले साल मैंने छुट्टी नहीं ली
opts.gu: ગયા વર્ષે મેં રજા ન લીધી

opts.t: 休みはなかなか取れないものだ
opts.r: yasumi wa nakanaka torenai mono da
opts.en: it's hard to actually take time off

opts.t: 1か月ぐらい休みを取りたい
opts.en: I want to take about a month off
opts.hi: मैं लगभग एक महीने की छुट्टी लेना चाहता हूँ
opts.gu: હું લગભગ એક મહિનાની રજા લેવા માગું છું

items.why: b) is a general evaluation (〜ものだ) that contradicts "there's paid leave" → "but you can't really use it". a) is a single past fact — the book says the second half is not a mere fact. c) is a wish that actually follows from having leave, so there's no contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: このテーブルは高いとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono teeburu wa takai to wa ie, (___).
items.en: This table may be expensive, but it's something you can use for a lifetime.
items.hi: माना कि यह मेज़ महँगी है, फिर भी यह ज़िंदगी भर काम आने वाली चीज़ है।
items.gu: માન્યું કે આ ટેબલ મોંઘું છે, છતાં તે આખી જિંદગી ચાલે એવી વસ્તુ છે.

opts.en: it's something you can use all your life

opts.t: わたしは思い切って買った
opts.en: I took the plunge and bought it

items.why: a) is the speaker's evaluation that offsets "expensive" ("but worth it"). b) and c) are both narrated events, not evaluations; and c) "it broke quickly" doesn't answer "expensive" with a judgment that outweighs it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）といえども、勉強していなければいい点はとれないだろう。
items.qr: (___) to iedomo, benkyou shite inakereba ii ten wa torenai darou.
items.en: Even if it's an easy test, you probably won't get a good score without studying.
items.hi: भले ही परीक्षा आसान हो, बिना पढ़े अच्छे अंक नहीं मिलेंगे।
items.gu: ભલે પરીક્ષા સહેલી હોય, વાંચ્યા વગર સારા ગુણ નહીં મળે.
items.why: といえども overturns what you'd normally expect from X (そこから普通に予想されること). An easy test → you'd expect a good score → "but not without study". a) a first test and c) an entrance exam don't create the expectation "you'll score well anyway", so there's nothing to deny.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 失業したといえども、（ ）。
items.qr: Shitsugyou shita to iedomo, (___).
items.en: Even though you've lost your job, you mustn't fall behind on the rent.
items.hi: भले ही नौकरी छूट गई हो, किराया बकाया नहीं रखना चाहिए।
items.gu: ભલે નોકરી છૂટી ગઈ હોય, ભાડું બાકી ન રાખવું જોઈએ.

opts.t: 家賃を滞納してはいけない
opts.r: yachin o tainou shite wa ikenai
opts.en: you mustn't fall behind on rent

opts.t: 彼はまた高い車を買った
opts.r: kare wa mata takai kuruma o katta
opts.hi: उसने फिर एक महँगी गाड़ी ख़रीदी

items.why: The second half of といえども is mainly an obligation / resolve / assertion, and it goes against the natural expectation ("jobless → you might be excused for not paying"). a) does both. b) is a narrated event (and about 彼, not a rule). c) is a command that simply follows from losing your job — no contrast.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 犯人でない証拠があるといえども、彼のことを（ ）。
items.qr: Hannin de nai shouko ga aru to iedomo, kare no koto o (___).
items.en: Even though there's evidence he isn't the culprit, we need to look into him.
items.hi: भले ही सबूत है कि वह अपराधी नहीं है, फिर भी उसकी जाँच करना ज़रूरी है।
items.gu: ભલે પુરાવો છે કે તે ગુનેગાર નથી, છતાં તેની તપાસ કરવી જરૂરી છે.

opts.r: ki ni suru no desu ka
opts.hi: क्या आप उसकी चिंता करते हैं?
opts.gu: શું તમે તેની ચિંતા કરો છો?

opts.t: 調べてみる必要がある

items.why: c) is an obligation/assertion (〜必要がある) — the typical ending for といえども — and it defies the expectation "proof of innocence → leave him alone". a) is a request and b) is a question; neither is the speaker's firm statement the stiff といえども calls for.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 彼女のお母さんだから、きっと静かな人だと思いきや、（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo no okaasan da kara, kitto shizuka na hito da to omoiki ya, (___).
items.en: Since she's her mother, I assumed she'd be a quiet person — but she turned out to be very lively.
items.hi: उसकी माँ हैं, इसलिए सोचा था ज़रूर शांत स्वभाव की होंगी, पर वे तो बहुत चहकने वाली निकलीं।
items.gu: તેની મા છે, એટલે ધાર્યું હતું કે ચોક્કસ શાંત સ્વભાવનાં હશે, પણ તેઓ તો બહુ બોલકાં નીકળ્યાં.

opts.t: とてもにぎやかな人だった
opts.en: she was a very lively person

opts.t: やはりとても静かな人だった
opts.r: yahari totemo shizuka na hito datta
opts.en: as expected, she was very quiet
opts.hi: जैसा सोचा था, वे बहुत शांत थीं
opts.gu: ધાર્યા મુજબ, તેઓ બહુ શાંત હતાં

opts.t: とてもきれいな人だった

items.why: と思いきや must be followed by a result different from the expectation. quiet → lively is the direct reversal. b) (やはり) confirms the expectation. c) is on a different axis (looks, not personality), so it doesn't contradict "quiet".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: お酒好きの松本さんは甘い物なんか好きじゃないと思いきや、（ ）。
items.qr: Osakezuki no Matsumoto-san wa amai mono nanka suki ja nai to omoiki ya, (___).
items.en: I assumed Mr. Matsumoto, who loves his drink, wouldn't care for sweets — but he ate as many as three pieces of cake.
items.hi: सोचा था शराब के शौक़ीन मात्सुमोतो जी को मिठाई-विठाई पसंद नहीं होगी, पर उन्होंने तो तीन-तीन केक खा लिए।
items.gu: ધાર્યું હતું કે દારૂના શોખીન માત્સુમોતોજીને મીઠાઈ-બીઠાઈ નહીં ગમતી હોય, પણ તેમણે તો ત્રણ-ત્રણ કેક ખાઈ લીધી.

opts.t: 辛いものばかり食べた
opts.en: he ate nothing but spicy food

opts.t: ケーキは食べないと言った
opts.en: he said he wouldn't eat cake
opts.hi: उन्होंने कहा कि केक नहीं खाएँगे
opts.gu: તેમણે કહ્યું કે કેક નહીં ખાય

opts.t: ケーキを三つも食べた
opts.en: he ate three pieces of cake

items.why: Expectation: "doesn't like sweets". Only c) reverses it (and 三つも adds the surprise). a) and b) both confirm the expectation, so there is no 意外感 for と思いきや to express.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: あの弱小チーム、1回戦で負けると思いきや（ ）。
items.qr: Ano jakushou chiimu, ikkaisen de makeru to omoiki ya (___).
items.en: That weak little team — I thought they'd lose in the first round, but they made it all the way to the final.
items.hi: वह कमज़ोर टीम — सोचा था पहले ही दौर में हार जाएगी, पर वह तो फ़ाइनल तक पहुँच गई।
items.gu: તે નબળી ટીમ — ધાર્યું હતું કે પહેલા જ રાઉન્ડમાં હારી જશે, પણ તે તો ફાઇનલ સુધી પહોંચી ગઈ.

opts.en: as expected, they lost in round one
opts.hi: जैसा सोचा था, पहले दौर में हार गई
opts.gu: ધાર્યા મુજબ, પહેલા રાઉન્ડમાં હારી ગઈ

opts.t: だれも勝つとは思わなかった
opts.r: dare mo katsu to wa omowanakatta
opts.hi: किसी ने नहीं सोचा था कि वह जीतेगी
opts.gu: કોઈએ ધાર્યું નહોતું કે તે જીતશે

items.why: The second half must be the actual result that differed from the expectation — c). a) confirms the expectation (やはり). b) is just another expectation, not a result, and it agrees with the first half.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: いくつか間違いがある（ ）、トム君の日本語の文章は素晴らしい。
items.qr: Ikutsu ka machigai ga aru (___), Tomu-kun no Nihongo no bunshou wa subarashii.
items.en: Granted there are a few mistakes, but Tom's Japanese writing is excellent.
items.hi: माना कि कुछ ग़लतियाँ हैं, फिर भी टॉम का जापानी लेखन शानदार है।
items.gu: માન્યું કે થોડી ભૂલો છે, છતાં ટૉમનું જાપાની લખાણ ઉત્તમ છે.
items.why: Fact (there are mistakes) + speaker's contrary evaluation (素晴らしい) = とはいえ. b) ものを needs a counter-to-fact supposition and a regret. c) と思いきや needs an expectation, and "there are mistakes" is a fact, not something the speaker had wrongly assumed.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 今日は一日中晴れる（ ）、午後からざあざあ降りになった。
items.qr: Kyou wa ichinichijuu hareru (___), gogo kara zaazaaburi ni natta.
items.en: I thought it would be sunny all day today, but from the afternoon it poured.
items.hi: सोचा था आज दिन भर धूप रहेगी, पर दोपहर से मूसलाधार बारिश होने लगी।
items.gu: ધાર્યું હતું કે આજે આખો દિવસ તડકો રહેશે, પણ બપોરથી ધોધમાર વરસાદ પડવા લાગ્યો.
items.why: 一日中晴れる is an expectation that turned out wrong, and the second half is the surprising actual result → と思いきや. a) とはいえ and b) といっても both need the first half to be a fact; "it will be sunny all day" never became true.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 事情を知らなかった（ ）、失礼な質問をしてしまいました。
items.qr: Jijou o shiranakatta (___), shitsurei na shitsumon o shite shimaimashita.
items.en: Although I didn't know the circumstances, I asked a rude question (and I'm sorry).
items.hi: माना कि मुझे हालात की जानकारी नहीं थी, फिर भी मैंने बेअदबी भरा सवाल पूछ लिया।
items.gu: માન્યું કે મને પરિસ્થિતિની ખબર નહોતી, છતાં મેં અવિવેકી સવાલ પૂછી નાખ્યો.
items.why: Same shape as the book's 【3】④ (仕方がなかったとはいえ、ご迷惑をおかけしました): an admitted fact/excuse + "still, I was in the wrong". a) ところを needs the listener's ongoing situation (お忙しいところを); 知らなかった is the speaker's own ignorance. b) ものを would need a counterfactual (知っていれば…しなかったものを).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: もっとちゃんと薬を飲めば早く（ ）。
items.qr: Motto chanto kusuri o nomeba hayaku (___).
items.en: If you'd taken your medicine properly, you'd have got better sooner.
items.hi: दवा ठीक से ली होती तो जल्दी ठीक हो जाते।
items.gu: દવા બરાબર લીધી હોત તો જલદી સાજા થઈ જાત.

opts.hi: माना कि ठीक हो गए, फिर भी

items.why: 〜ば…た + ものを at the end of the sentence, with the reality left unsaid — exactly the book's 【2】④ (手伝ったものを。). a) and c) must be followed by another clause, but the sentence ends at the blank; they also need the first part to be a fact, not a supposition.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: その計画は意義がある（ ）、多くの人の支持は得られないだろう。
items.qr: Sono keikaku wa igi ga aru (___), ooku no hito no shiji wa erarenai darou.
items.en: Even though the plan is worthwhile, it probably won't win the support of many people.
items.hi: भले ही वह योजना सार्थक है, फिर भी उसे बहुत लोगों का समर्थन नहीं मिलेगा।
items.gu: ભલે તે યોજના અર્થપૂર્ણ છે, છતાં તેને ઘણા લોકોનું સમર્થન નહીં મળે.
items.why: A fact (it has merit) whose natural expectation (people will back it) is denied by the speaker's assertion (〜だろう) → といえども. a) ものを needs a counterfactual supposition. c) と思いきや needs an already-happened surprising result; 〜得られないだろう is only a prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: （ ）よく来てくださいました。
items.qr: (___) yoku kite kudasaimashita.
items.en: Thank you so much for coming all this way.
items.hi: इतनी दूर से आने के लिए आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।
items.gu: આટલે દૂરથી આવવા બદલ આપનો ખૂબ ખૂબ આભાર.
items.why: A set courtesy phrase of thanks for the trouble taken (遠いところを／お忙しいところを) — 〜ところを. b) といえども is stiff and leads to an obligation or assertion, not to thanks. c) ものを expresses regret about a counterfactual, which makes no sense in a welcome.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: わたしは、その仕事を引き受けるとは（ ）、結局やれなかった。
items.qr: Watashi wa, sono shigoto o hikiukeru to wa (___), kekkyoku yarenakatta.
items.en: I did say I'd take on the job, but in the end I couldn't do it.
items.hi: मैंने वह काम लेने की बात तो कही थी, पर आख़िरकार कर नहीं पाया।
items.gu: મેં તે કામ લેવાની વાત તો કરી હતી, પણ આખરે કરી શક્યો નહીં.

opts.hi: माना कि कहा था, फिर भी

opts.en: I'd have said it, if only…

items.why: 〜ものの is the N2 form from the 〔復習〕 box: "I did X, but what should have followed didn't" — a plain narrative contrast between two facts. a) とはいえ needs a speaker's evaluation after it, but 結局やれなかった is just a fact. c) ものを needs a counterfactual supposition (〜ば…たものを); here 言った really happened. Note the trap: ものの vs ものを differ by one kana.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 8課 · 逆接

items.q: 必要な学費とあれば、（ ）。
items.qr: Hitsuyou na gakuhi to areba, (___).
items.en: If it's tuition I actually need, my father will probably pay it for me.
items.hi: अगर बात ज़रूरी फ़ीस की हो, तो पिताजी शायद भर देंगे।
items.gu: જો વાત જરૂરી ફીની હોય, તો પિતાજી કદાચ ભરી આપશે.

opts.t: どうか払ってください
父は払ってくれるだろう

opts.r: dare ga harau n desu ka

items.why: After とあれば comes the speaker's wish, intention or judgment. b) is a judgment (〜だろう). a) is a request to the listener and c) is a question — neither is the speaker's own stance.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: （ ）とあれば、精いっぱい頑張ります。
items.qr: (___) to areba, seiippai ganbarimasu.
items.en: If it's a request from you, I'll do my very best.
items.hi: अगर आपका अनुरोध है, तो मैं पूरी जान लगा दूँगा।
items.gu: જો તમારી વિનંતી છે, તો હું પૂરેપૂરી મહેનત કરીશ.
items.why: とあれば needs a special condition (特別な条件) that motivates the result: "since it's you asking, I'll give it everything". a) everyday housework is the opposite of special. b) driving is just an activity, not a reason that would make someone try their hardest.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 家族のためとあれば、（ ）。
items.qr: Kazoku no tame to areba, (___).
items.en: If it's for his family, he'll probably do anything.
items.hi: अगर परिवार के लिए हो, तो वह शायद कुछ भी कर गुज़रेगा।
items.gu: જો પરિવાર માટે હોય, તો તે કદાચ કંઈ પણ કરી છૂટશે.

opts.t: どんなことをするんですか
opts.r: donna koto o suru n desu ka
opts.en: what kind of thing will you do?

opts.t: わたしに何ができますか
opts.r: watashi ni nani ga dekimasu ka

opts.t: 彼はどんなことでもするだろう
opts.r: kare wa donna koto de mo suru darou

items.why: Same rule — the second clause is the speaker's judgment (〜だろう). a) and b) are questions; とあれば doesn't lead into asking someone something.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: あんな人が委員長に（ ）最後、この会はだめになる。
items.qr: Anna hito ga iinchou ni (___) saigo, kono kai wa dame ni naru.
items.en: If someone like that becomes chair, this association is finished.
items.hi: अगर वैसा आदमी अध्यक्ष बन गया, तो बस, यह संस्था बर्बाद हो जाएगी।
items.gu: જો એવો માણસ અધ્યક્ષ બની ગયો, તો બસ, આ મંડળ બરબાદ થઈ જશે.
items.why: The fixed shape is た形 + ら最後 (or た形 + が最後): なったら最後. a) 〜と and b) 〜ば are other conditional forms that never combine with 最後.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 彼は怒ったら最後、（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa okottara saigo, (___).
items.en: Once he gets angry, that's it — he'll never forgive you.
items.hi: एक बार वह नाराज़ हो गया तो बस, कभी माफ़ नहीं करता।
items.gu: એક વાર તે ગુસ્સે થયો તો બસ, ક્યારેય માફ નથી કરતો.

opts.t: 次の日にはもう忘れている
opts.r: tsugi no hi ni wa mou wasurete iru
opts.en: by the next day he's forgotten
opts.hi: अगले दिन तक भूल चुका होता है
opts.gu: બીજા દિવસ સુધીમાં ભૂલી ગયો હોય છે

opts.t: 絶対に許してくれない

items.why: 〜たら最後 is followed by something the speaker sees as very bad and lasting. c) "never forgives" fits. a) forgetting by the next day is actually a good outcome. b) a scary face is a natural, mild, momentary reaction — not the irreversible "end" that 最後 implies.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 麻薬は恐ろしいものだ。一度使ったが最後（ ）。
items.qr: Mayaku wa osoroshii mono da. Ichido tsukatta ga saigo (___).
items.en: Drugs are terrifying. Use them once and you can no longer stop by willpower alone.
items.hi: नशीली दवाएँ बहुत भयानक होती हैं। एक बार इस्तेमाल किया तो बस, अपनी इच्छा-शक्ति से छोड़ नहीं पाते।
items.gu: નશીલા પદાર્થો બહુ ભયાનક હોય છે. એક વાર વાપર્યા તો બસ, પોતાની ઇચ્છાશક્તિથી છોડી શકાતા નથી.

opts.t: 意志があればやめられる
opts.hi: इच्छा-शक्ति हो तो छोड़ सकते हैं

opts.t: 自分の意志ではやめられなくなる
opts.r: jibun no ishi de wa yamerarenaku naru
opts.en: you can't stop by your own will
opts.hi: अपनी मर्ज़ी से छोड़ नहीं पाते

opts.t: 医者に相談したほうがいい
opts.r: isha ni soudan shita hou ga ii

items.why: The second clause must describe the terrible, irreversible situation — b). a) is reassuring, which contradicts 恐ろしい and 最後. c) is advice, not a description of the bad state that results.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしは卵アレルギーなので、卵が入っている食品をうっかり口にしたら最後、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa tamago arerugii na node, tamago ga haitte iru shokuhin o ukkari kuchi ni shitara saigo, (___).
items.en: I'm allergic to eggs, so if I accidentally eat anything containing egg, I break out in red spots all over my face.
items.hi: मुझे अंडे से एलर्जी है, इसलिए ग़लती से अंडे वाली कोई चीज़ खा ली तो बस, पूरे चेहरे पर लाल दाने निकल आते हैं।
items.gu: મને ઈંડાંની એલર્જી છે, એટલે ભૂલથી ઈંડાંવાળી કોઈ વસ્તુ ખાઈ લીધી તો બસ, આખા ચહેરા પર લાલ ફોલ્લીઓ થઈ જાય છે.

opts.t: 顔中に赤いぶつぶつができる
opts.r: kaojuu ni akai butsubutsu ga dekiru
opts.en: red spots appear all over my face
opts.hi: पूरे चेहरे पर लाल दाने निकल आते हैं
opts.gu: આખા ચહેરા પર લાલ ફોલ્લીઓ થાય છે

opts.en: I absolutely don't want to eat it

items.why: The result after 〜たら最後 is the bad event that inevitably follows — the allergic reaction, b). a) is the speaker's own countermeasure, not the disaster. c) is a wish, and it makes no sense after having already eaten it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: サラリーマンが毎日会社に（ ）ではだめだ。
items.qr: Sarariiman ga mainichi kaisha ni (___) de wa dame da.
items.en: An office worker who's late for work every day is hopeless.
items.hi: अगर कोई नौकरीपेशा रोज़ दफ़्तर देर से पहुँचे, तो यह नहीं चलेगा।
items.gu: જો કોઈ નોકરિયાત રોજ ઑફિસ મોડો પહોંચે, તો એ ન ચાલે.
items.why: The connection is plain form + ようでは: 遅刻するようでは. b) and c) use the volitional ending 〜(よ)う, which looks similar but is a different form entirely — it can't be followed by では.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 寄付の手続きがこんなに（ ）ようでは、寄付をする人が少なくなってしまう。
items.qr: Kifu no tetsuzuki ga konna ni (___) you de wa, kifu o suru hito ga sukunaku natte shimau.
items.en: If the donation procedure is this much of a hassle, fewer people will donate.
items.hi: अगर दान की प्रक्रिया इतनी झंझट भरी है, तो दान करने वाले कम हो जाएँगे।
items.gu: જો દાનની પ્રક્રિયા આટલી ઝંઝટવાળી છે, તો દાન કરનારા ઓછા થઈ જશે.
items.why: The 🔗 line: ナ形 だ −な (or −である) + ようでは. So 面倒なようでは (or 面倒であるようでは). a) the bare stem can't attach to よう; c) だ must be dropped.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 仕事がそんなに忙しいようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Shigoto ga sonna ni isogashii you de wa, (___).
items.en: If your work is that busy, you'll ruin your health.
items.hi: अगर काम इतना ज़्यादा है, तो तबीयत बिगड़ जाएगी।
items.gu: જો કામ આટલું બધું છે, તો તબિયત બગડી જશે.

opts.t: 毎日充実しているでしょう

items.why: 〜ようでは predicts an undesirable result. a) is that warning. b) and c) treat being busy as something good — the opposite of what ようでは expresses.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 敬語がちゃんと使えないようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Keigo ga chanto tsukaenai you de wa, (___).
items.en: If you can't use honorific language properly, you can't do customer-service work.
items.hi: अगर आदरसूचक भाषा ठीक से नहीं बोल पाते, तो ग्राहक-सेवा का काम नहीं कर सकते।
items.gu: જો આદરસૂચક ભાષા બરાબર બોલી નથી શકતા, તો ગ્રાહક-સેવાનું કામ ન કરી શકો.

opts.t: しっかり勉強しなさい
接客の仕事はできない
opts.hi: ग्राहक-सेवा का काम नहीं कर सकते

opts.t: 日本人に聞いたほうがいい
opts.r: Nihonjin ni kiita hou ga ii
opts.en: you'd better ask a Japanese person
opts.hi: किसी जापानी से पूछ लेना बेहतर है

items.why: The ⚠ note: what follows is a prediction that something undesirable will happen. b) is exactly that. a) is a command and c) is advice — they tell the listener what to do instead of predicting the bad outcome.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 一日中アニメばかり見ているようでは、（ ）。
items.qr: Ichinichijuu anime bakari mite iru you de wa, (___).
items.en: If you watch nothing but anime all day, you won't have any time to study.
items.hi: अगर दिन भर सिर्फ़ एनिमे ही देखते रहोगे, तो पढ़ने का समय ही नहीं बचेगा।
items.gu: જો આખો દિવસ ફક્ત એનિમે જ જોતા રહેશો, તો ભણવાનો સમય જ નહીં બચે.

opts.t: アニメの専門家になれますよ
opts.r: anime no senmonka ni naremasu yo
opts.en: you could become an anime expert
opts.hi: तुम एनिमे के विशेषज्ञ बन सकते हो

opts.t: 勉強する時間がないでしょう
opts.r: benkyou suru jikan ga nai deshou
opts.en: you won't have time to study

opts.t: アニメの学校に行くといいですよ
opts.r: anime no gakkou ni iku to ii desu yo
opts.en: you should go to an anime school

items.why: b) is an undesirable prediction (〜でしょう). a) is a positive outcome, which clashes with ようでは's "bad state → bad result". c) is a suggestion, not a prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 住民の理解と協力なしには（ ）。
items.qr: Juumin no rikai to kyouryoku nashi ni wa (___).
items.en: Without the residents' understanding and cooperation, this plan can't be carried out.
items.hi: निवासियों की समझ और सहयोग के बिना यह योजना लागू नहीं हो सकती।
items.gu: રહેવાસીઓની સમજ અને સહકાર વિના આ યોજના અમલમાં મૂકી શકાય નહીં.

opts.t: この計画は実行できない
opts.en: this plan can't be carried out
opts.hi: यह योजना लागू नहीं हो सकती
opts.gu: આ યોજના અમલમાં મૂકી શકાય નહીં

items.why: なしには must be followed by a negative expression saying the thing can't be achieved. a) does that. b) is affirmative (and describes a side effect, not an impossibility). c) is volition.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 国の援助なしでは（ ）。
items.qr: Kuni no enjo nashi de wa (___).
items.en: Without government aid, this research can't continue.
items.hi: सरकारी सहायता के बिना यह शोध जारी नहीं रह सकता।
items.gu: સરકારી સહાય વિના આ સંશોધન ચાલુ રહી શકે નહીં.

opts.t: 民間の企業から寄付をしてもらおう
opts.r: minkan no kigyou kara kifu o shite moraou
opts.en: let's get donations from private companies
opts.hi: चलो निजी कंपनियों से दान लें
opts.gu: ચાલો ખાનગી કંપનીઓ પાસેથી દાન લઈએ

opts.t: わたしはこの研究班を辞める
opts.r: watashi wa kono kenkyuuhan o yameru
opts.hi: मैं यह शोध दल छोड़ दूँगा
opts.gu: હું આ સંશોધન ટુકડી છોડી દઈશ

opts.t: この研究は続けられない
opts.hi: यह शोध जारी नहीं रह सकता
opts.gu: આ સંશોધન ચાલુ ન રહી શકે

items.why: The aid is presented as indispensable, so the ending states what becomes impossible without it — c). a) is volition (〜よう) and b) is the speaker's decision; neither is the negative "can't happen" that なしでは requires.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: しっかり準備することなくしては（ ）。
items.qr: Shikkari junbi suru koto nakushite wa (___).
items.en: Without thorough preparation, you can't give a good presentation.
items.hi: अच्छी तैयारी के बिना अच्छी प्रस्तुति नहीं दी जा सकती।
items.gu: સારી તૈયારી વિના સારું પ્રેઝન્ટેશન આપી શકાય નહીં.

opts.en: you can't give a good presentation

opts.t: いい発表ができるんですか
opts.r: ii happyou ga dekiru n desu ka
opts.en: can you give a good presentation?
opts.hi: क्या अच्छी प्रस्तुति हो सकती है?

opts.t: 発表するのはやめよう

items.why: Negative ending required — a). b) is a question and c) is volition; both break the "X is essential, so without it Y is impossible" structure.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 結婚して（ ）くらいなら、一人で暮らすほうがましだ。
items.qr: Kekkon shite (___) kurai nara, hitori de kurasu hou ga mashi da.
items.en: If getting married means losing my freedom, I'd rather live alone.
items.hi: शादी करके आज़ादी खोने से तो अकेले रहना बेहतर है।
items.gu: લગ્ન કરીને આઝાદી ગુમાવવા કરતાં તો એકલા રહેવું સારું.
items.why: くらいなら attaches to the dictionary form of a verb describing the worst case. b) is both. c) is the past (た形), which the 🔗 line doesn't allow. a) "wanting freedom" isn't a bad situation to avoid, and 欲しい is an adjective.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしは料理が苦手なんです。自分で作るくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa ryouri ga nigate nan desu. Jibun de tsukuru kurai nara, (___).
items.en: I'm hopeless at cooking. Rather than cook for myself, I'd be fine with just bread every day.
items.hi: मुझे खाना बनाना बिल्कुल नहीं आता। ख़ुद बनाने से तो रोज़ सिर्फ़ ब्रेड खाना भी चलेगा।
items.gu: મને રસોઈ બિલકુલ નથી આવડતી. જાતે બનાવવા કરતાં તો રોજ ફક્ત બ્રેડ ખાવી પણ ચાલશે.

opts.t: おいしくできるわけがありません
opts.en: there's no way it'll taste good
opts.hi: स्वादिष्ट बनने का सवाल ही नहीं
opts.gu: સ્વાદિષ્ટ બને એવો સવાલ જ નથી

opts.t: 料理教室に行って料理を習います
opts.r: ryouri kyoushitsu ni itte ryouri o naraimasu
opts.hi: कुकिंग क्लास जाकर खाना बनाना सीखूँगा

opts.t: 毎日パンだけでもいいです
opts.r: mainichi pan dake de mo ii desu
opts.en: just bread every day is fine

items.why: The second clause is the option the speaker considers better than the worst case (cooking for herself). c) is that lesser evil. a) is a consequence of cooking, not an alternative to it. b) means she would cook after all — it doesn't avoid the worst case.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: わたしはエアコンが嫌いだ。エアコンを入れるくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa eakon ga kirai da. Eakon o ireru kurai nara, (___).
items.en: I hate air-conditioning. Rather than turn it on, I'll put up with the heat.
items.hi: मुझे एसी पसंद नहीं। एसी चलाने से तो गर्मी सह लेना बेहतर है।
items.gu: મને એસી ગમતું નથી. એસી ચાલુ કરવા કરતાં તો ગરમી સહન કરી લઉં.

opts.en: I'll put up with the heat

opts.hi: बिजली का बिल बढ़ जाता है
कमरा बहुत ठंडा हो जाता है

items.why: a) is the alternative the speaker prefers. b) and c) are consequences of turning on the air-conditioner — they would follow 〜と／〜たら, not くらいなら.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: あんな人に頭を下げて頼むくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Anna hito ni atama o sagete tanomu kurai nara, (___).
items.en: Rather than bow my head and beg someone like that, I'll do it myself.
items.hi: वैसे आदमी के आगे सिर झुकाकर विनती करने से तो मैं ख़ुद ही कर लूँगा।
items.gu: એવા માણસ સામે માથું નમાવીને વિનંતી કરવા કરતાં તો હું જાતે જ કરી લઈશ.

opts.t: 彼はいい気分になるだろう
opts.r: kare wa ii kibun ni naru darou

opts.t: だれもやってくれないだろう
opts.en: nobody will do it for me

items.why: b) is the preferable alternative chosen instead of the worst case (begging). a) is a consequence of begging. c) is a prediction, not an alternative the speaker would prefer.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: おいしいものを（ ）、わたしはダイエットなんかしなくてもいい。
items.qr: Oishii mono o (___), watashi wa daietto nanka shinakute mo ii.
items.en: If it means giving up delicious food, I don't need to diet at all.
items.hi: स्वादिष्ट खाने से परहेज़ करने से तो अच्छा है कि मैं डाइटिंग करूँ ही नहीं।
items.gu: સ્વાદિષ્ટ ખાવાનું ટાળવા કરતાં તો સારું કે હું ડાયેટિંગ કરું જ નહીં.

opts.en: if it's a matter of holding back
opts.hi: अगर परहेज़ की बात हो तो

opts.en: if (you're in the bad state of) holding back
opts.hi: अगर परहेज़ करने की हालत है तो
opts.gu: જો પરેજી કરવાની હાલત હોય તો

items.why: Worst case (giving up tasty food) → lesser evil (not dieting) = くらいなら. a) とあれば needs a special condition that justifies the speaker's action. b) ようでは needs a predicted bad result; "I don't have to diet" isn't one.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: ここでやる気を（ ）、彼は再び立ち上がれなくなるだろう。
items.qr: Koko de yaruki o (___), kare wa futatabi tachiagarenaku naru darou.
items.en: If he loses his motivation now, that'll be it — he'll probably never get back on his feet.
items.hi: अगर अभी उसका हौसला टूट गया, तो बस, वह शायद फिर कभी उठ नहीं पाएगा।
items.gu: જો અત્યારે તેનો ઉત્સાહ તૂટી ગયો, તો બસ, તે કદાચ ફરી ક્યારેય ઊભો નહીં થઈ શકે.

opts.en: once he loses it, that's it
if it's a matter of losing it
opts.hi: अगर खोने की बात हो तो

items.why: A trigger followed by an irreversible disaster (never getting up again) = たら最後. b) とあれば wants a special condition justifying an action. c) くらいなら needs a preferable alternative in the second half, not a dire prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: （ ）、どんなことでもするんですか。
items.qr: (___), donna koto de mo suru n desu ka.
items.en: So if it's to make money, you'll do anything at all?
items.hi: यानी अगर पैसा कमाने की बात हो, तो आप कुछ भी कर लेंगे?
items.gu: એટલે જો પૈસા કમાવાની વાત હોય, તો તમે કંઈ પણ કરી લેશો?

opts.t: 金もうけするくらいなら

opts.hi: अगर पैसा कमाने की बात हो तो
opts.gu: જો પૈસા કમાવાની વાત હોય તો

opts.en: once you've made money, that's it

items.why: "If it's (for the special purpose of) money, (you'd do) anything" = とあれば, with どんなことでも as in the book's 【1】①. This is a rhetorical, critical question to the listener — it repeats the listener's stance back to them, so it doesn't break the "no questions" tendency in the way [1] Q3's genuine questions do. a) くらいなら would make money-making the worst case. c) たら最後 would need a disaster after it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 患者の気持ちを（ ）いい医者にはなれないだろう。
items.qr: Kanja no kimochi o (___) ii isha ni wa narenai darou.
items.en: Without understanding patients' feelings, you can't become a good doctor.
items.hi: मरीज़ों की भावनाओं को समझे बिना कोई अच्छा डॉक्टर नहीं बन सकता।
items.gu: દર્દીઓની લાગણી સમજ્યા વિના કોઈ સારો ડૉક્ટર બની શકે નહીં.

opts.hi: न समझने की बात करें तो

opts.t: 理解しなかったら最後
opts.en: once you fail to understand, that's it

opts.t: 理解することなくして

items.why: Understanding is the indispensable condition, and a negative (なれない) follows → V-dictionary + こと + なくして. a) といえば changes the topic, and makes no sense here. b) たら最後 needs a single trigger event leading to disaster; "failing to understand" is a lasting attitude, and 最後 sounds odd with a negative trigger.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: 生まれたばかりなのに、今から子育てが大変なんて（ ）この先やっていけませんよ。
items.qr: Umareta bakari na noni, ima kara kosodate ga taihen nante (___) kono saki yatte ikemasen yo.
items.en: The baby's only just been born — if you're already saying child-rearing is tough, you won't cope with what's ahead.
items.hi: बच्चा अभी-अभी पैदा हुआ है, और अगर तुम अभी से कह रहे हो कि पालना मुश्किल है, तो आगे कैसे निभाओगे?
items.gu: બાળક હમણાં જ જન્મ્યું છે, અને જો તમે અત્યારથી જ કહો છો કે ઉછેરવું મુશ્કેલ છે, તો આગળ કેવી રીતે નિભાવશો?

opts.hi: अगर (अभी से) कह रहे हो तो

items.why: An undesirable present state (already complaining) → a predicted bad result (you won't cope) = ようでは, exactly like 【3】②. b) なくして would make "saying it's hard" something indispensable — nonsense. c) くらいなら needs a preferable alternative, but やっていけません is a negative prediction.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 9課 · 条件

items.q: この仕事はだれが（ ）と、大差ない。
items.qr: Kono shigoto wa dare ga (___) to, taisa nai.
items.en: It makes little difference who does this job.
items.hi: यह काम कोई भी करे, ज़्यादा फ़र्क़ नहीं पड़ता।
items.gu: આ કામ કોઈ પણ કરે, ખાસ ફરક પડતો નથી.

opts.en: so as to do / like doing

items.why: Verbs take the volitional form (う・よう形) before と: しようと. a) するよう is the "manner/so that" よう, a different word. c) だろう + と is only for adjectives and nouns (困難だろうと); a verb uses its own volitional form instead.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 母は、どんなに（ ）が、払うべき金は払ってくれた。
items.qr: Haha wa, donna ni (___) ga, harau beki kane wa haratte kureta.
items.en: However expensive it was, my mother always paid what needed to be paid.
items.hi: चाहे कितना भी महँगा हो, माँ ने जो पैसे भरने ज़रूरी थे वे भर दिए।
items.gu: ભલે ગમે તેટલું મોંઘું હોય, માએ જે પૈસા ભરવા જરૂરી હતા તે ભરી આપ્યા.
items.why: The 🔗 line: イ形 かろう + と(も)・が → 高かろうが. a) 高いだろう is the pattern for な-adjectives/nouns (〜だろう), not い-adjectives. c) 高かったろう is a past conjecture, not on the connection line.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 母がどんなに説得しようが、父は（ ）。
items.qr: Haha ga donna ni settoku shiyou ga, chichi wa (___).
items.en: No matter how hard my mother tried to persuade him, my father didn't change his mind.
items.hi: माँ ने चाहे कितना भी समझाया, पिताजी ने अपना विचार नहीं बदला।
items.gu: માએ ગમે તેટલું સમજાવ્યું, પિતાજીએ પોતાનો વિચાર ન બદલ્યો.
items.why: The second clause must show the result is not affected by the condition (前の条件に影響されない). c) does. b) means he was affected. a) is unrelated to whether the persuasion had any effect.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: どんなに便利なものだろうと、（ ）。
items.qr: Donna ni benri na mono darou to, (___).
items.en: However convenient something may be, I don't want to buy things I don't need.
items.hi: चीज़ चाहे कितनी भी काम की हो, जिसकी ज़रूरत नहीं वह मैं नहीं ख़रीदना चाहता।
items.gu: વસ્તુ ગમે તેટલી ઉપયોગી હોય, જેની જરૂર નથી તે હું ખરીદવા માગતો નથી.

opts.t: 要らないものは買いたくない
opts.en: I don't want to buy what I don't need
opts.hi: जिसकी ज़रूरत नहीं, वह नहीं ख़रीदना
opts.gu: જેની જરૂર નથી, તે નથી ખરીદવું

opts.t: 要らないものも買ってしまう
opts.en: I end up buying even what I don't need
opts.hi: बेज़रूरत चीज़ें भी ख़रीद लेता हूँ
opts.gu: બિનજરૂરી વસ્તુઓ પણ ખરીદી લઉં છું

items.why: "However convenient → I'm unmoved" — a) is the speaker's resolve, unaffected by convenience. b) shows the speaker being swayed by convenience, the opposite. c) is a general statement that has no connection with "however convenient".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: この先何があろうと、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono saki nani ga arou to, (___).
items.en: Whatever happens from here on, don't worry.
items.hi: आगे चाहे जो हो, चिंता मत करना।
items.gu: આગળ ગમે તે થાય, ચિંતા ન કરતો.

opts.r: shinpai de wa nai no ka

items.why: "Whatever happens" → a stance that ignores all possibilities: "don't worry" (the speaker's firm assertion). a) worrying is being affected by what might happen. c) is a question, not a judgment or resolve.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: わたしがあしたの会に参加しようとするまいと、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi ga ashita no kai ni sanka shiyou to suru mai to, (___).
items.en: Whether I go to tomorrow's meeting or not is none of your business, is it?
items.hi: मैं कल की बैठक में जाऊँ या न जाऊँ, इससे तुम्हारा क्या लेना-देना?
items.gu: હું કાલની મીટિંગમાં જાઉં કે ન જાઉં, તેમાં તારે શું લેવાદેવા?

opts.t: あなたはどうしますか
あなたもまだ決めていないのですか
opts.r: anata mo mada kimete inai no desu ka
opts.hi: क्या तुमने भी अभी तय नहीं किया?
opts.gu: શું તેં પણ હજી નક્કી નથી કર્યું?

opts.t: あなたには関係ないことでしょう
opts.r: anata ni wa kankei nai koto deshou
opts.en: it has nothing to do with you

items.why: "Whether I do or don't" → "it makes no difference (to you)": c) states exactly that. a) and b) are questions that treat my attendance as something that matters to the listener's plans — the opposite of 関係ない.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 信じようが（ ）、これは事実なのです。しっかり聞いてください。
items.qr: Shinjiyou ga (___), kore wa jijitsu na no desu. Shikkari kiite kudasai.
items.en: Whether you believe it or not, this is the truth. Please listen carefully.
items.hi: आप मानें या न मानें, यह सच है। ध्यान से सुनिए।
items.gu: તમે માનો કે ન માનો, આ હકીકત છે. ધ્યાનથી સાંભળો.
items.why: The ⚠ note: the same verb is repeated. 信じようが → 信じまいが (Group Ⅱ: stem 信じ + まい). a) and b) switch to a different verb, which breaks the "do or don't" pair.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: あの人はそばで人が聞いていようがいるまいが、（ ）。
items.qr: Ano hito wa soba de hito ga kiite iyou ga iru mai ga, (___).
items.en: Whether or not people nearby are listening, that person keeps talking in a loud voice.
items.hi: पास में कोई सुन रहा हो या न हो, वह आदमी ज़ोर-ज़ोर से बोलता ही रहता है।
items.gu: પાસે કોઈ સાંભળતું હોય કે ન હોય, તે માણસ જોરજોરથી બોલતો જ રહે છે.

opts.t: 大きい声でしゃべり続ける
声の大きさを時々変えて話す
opts.r: koe no ookisa o tokidoki kaete hanasu
opts.en: changes his volume now and then

items.why: The result must be unaffected by both possibilities: a) — he talks loudly regardless. b) suggests he adjusts depending on who is listening, and c) says he cares — both are affected by the condition.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: わたしは自分の小説が入賞しようとすまいと、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashi wa jibun no shousetsu ga nyuushou shiyou to su mai to, (___).
items.en: Whether or not my novel wins a prize, I'll keep on writing no matter what.
items.hi: मेरे उपन्यास को पुरस्कार मिले या न मिले, मैं तो बस लिखता रहूँगा।
items.gu: મારી નવલકથાને ઇનામ મળે કે ન મળે, હું તો બસ લખતો રહીશ.

opts.en: it's a turning point in my fate
opts.hi: यह मेरी क़िस्मत का मोड़ है

opts.t: どちらなのか心配で緊張している
opts.r: dochira na no ka shinpai de kinchou shite iru
opts.en: I'm nervous about which it'll be
opts.hi: क्या होगा, इसकी चिंता में घबराया हूँ
opts.gu: શું થશે, તેની ચિંતામાં ગભરાયેલો છું

items.why: c) is the speaker's resolve (決意), untouched by either outcome. a) says the outcome matters enormously, and b) shows the speaker anxious about the result — both contradict "whether or not". Note the する form: しようとすまいと (= するまいと).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: たとえ（ ）であれ、勉強が必要なときはするべきだ。
items.qr: Tatoe (___) de are, benkyou ga hitsuyou na toki wa suru beki da.
items.en: Even a distinguished professor should study when study is needed.
items.hi: चाहे कोई बड़ा प्रोफ़ेसर ही क्यों न हो, जब पढ़ाई ज़रूरी हो तो पढ़ना चाहिए।
items.gu: ભલે કોઈ મોટા પ્રોફેસર જ કેમ ન હોય, જ્યારે ભણવું જરૂરી હોય ત્યારે ભણવું જોઈએ.
items.why: たとえ〜であれ picks an extreme case that you might expect to be exempt — a great professor surely doesn't need to study? — and says "even then, no". b) students and c) children are exactly the people expected to study, so there is no "even" to express.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: たとえ（ ）であろうと、展示品をただで差し上げるわけにはいきません。
items.qr: Tatoe (___) de arou to, tenjihin o tada de sashiageru wake ni wa ikimasen.
items.en: Even if it's an amateur's work, we can't give exhibits away for free.
items.hi: चाहे किसी नौसिखिए की कृति ही क्यों न हो, प्रदर्शनी की चीज़ मुफ़्त में नहीं दी जा सकती।
items.gu: ભલે કોઈ શિખાઉની કૃતિ જ કેમ ન હોય, પ્રદર્શનની વસ્તુ મફતમાં આપી શકાય નહીં.
items.why: The noun must be the case where you'd expect giving it away free to be acceptable — an amateur piece seems low-value — and the sentence says "even so, no". With a) or b), refusing to give a valuable item away free is obvious; たとえ…であろうと would have nothing to overturn.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: どんな小さい企業であれ、（ ）。
items.qr: Donna chiisai kigyou de are, (___).
items.en: However small the company, you're lucky if you can get a job there.
items.hi: कंपनी चाहे कितनी भी छोटी हो, नौकरी मिल जाए तो क़िस्मत अच्छी है।
items.gu: કંપની ગમે તેટલી નાની હોય, નોકરી મળી જાય તો નસીબદાર કહેવાય.

opts.t: 今年は採用予定はない
opts.r: kotoshi wa saiyou yotei wa nai
opts.en: there are no hiring plans this year
opts.hi: इस साल भर्ती की कोई योजना नहीं
opts.gu: આ વર્ષે ભરતીની કોઈ યોજના નથી

opts.t: 就職できればラッキーだ
opts.en: you're lucky if you get a job
opts.hi: नौकरी मिल जाए तो क़िस्मत अच्छी

items.why: c) is a judgment that is not affected by the company's size ("small or not, it's lucky"). a) low pay is a consequence of being small — the condition does affect it. b) is a single fact about one company, not a judgment covering "however small".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: たとえ仲のいい友達であれ、今は（ ）。
items.qr: Tatoe naka no ii tomodachi de are, ima wa (___).
items.en: Even if it's a close friend, right now I can't trust anyone.
items.hi: चाहे कोई पक्का दोस्त ही क्यों न हो, अभी मैं किसी पर भरोसा नहीं कर सकता।
items.gu: ભલે કોઈ જિગરજાન મિત્ર જ કેમ ન હોય, અત્યારે હું કોઈના પર વિશ્વાસ નથી કરી શકતો.

opts.t: だれも信じることができない
opts.r: dare mo shinjiru koto ga dekinai
opts.hi: किसी पर भरोसा नहीं कर सकता
opts.gu: કોઈના પર વિશ્વાસ નથી કરી શકતો

opts.t: だれでも信じようと思う
opts.r: dare de mo shinjiyou to omou
opts.hi: मैं किसी पर भी भरोसा करना चाहता हूँ
opts.gu: હું કોઈના પર પણ વિશ્વાસ કરવા માગું છું

opts.t: だれでも信じられるのだ
opts.r: dare de mo shinjirareru no da
opts.hi: मैं किसी पर भी भरोसा कर सकता हूँ
opts.gu: હું કોઈના પર પણ વિશ્વાસ કરી શકું

items.why: "Even a close friend" — the case where you'd most expect trust — "still, no one". a) overturns that expectation. b) and c) say "I trust anyone", which wouldn't need たとえ…であれ (a close friend would naturally be trusted).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: このまま（ ）ところで、これ以上いいアイディアは出てこないだろう。
items.qr: Kono mama (___) tokoro de, kore ijou ii aidia wa dete konai darou.
items.en: Even if we go on thinking like this, no better idea is going to come out.
items.hi: इसी तरह सोचते भी रहें, तो इससे बेहतर कोई विचार नहीं निकलेगा।
items.gu: આમ જ વિચારતા રહીએ તો પણ, આનાથી સારો કોઈ વિચાર નહીં આવે.
items.why: 〜たところで = "even if you try ~, it's pointless". The action has to be the effort that turns out useless — continuing to think (このまま). a) and c) are "not thinking", and nobody would expect ideas from that, so calling it pointless says nothing.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 今さら真実を知ったところで、（ ）。
items.qr: Imasara shinjitsu o shitta tokoro de, (___).
items.en: Even if I learn the truth now, there's nothing that can be done about it anymore.
items.hi: अब सच जान भी लूँ, तो अब कुछ नहीं हो सकता।
items.gu: હવે સત્ય જાણી પણ લઉં, તો હવે કંઈ થઈ શકે નહીં.

opts.t: もうどうにもならない
opts.en: nothing can be done any more

opts.t: 方法はいくらでもある
opts.r: houhou wa ikura de mo aru
opts.en: there are any number of ways

items.why: After 〜たところで comes a negative judgment: a). b) is a request (働きかけ), which the ⚠ note rules out. c) is a positive judgment — the opposite of "pointless".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 反抗期の息子に何を説教したところで、（ ）。
items.qr: Hankouki no musuko ni nani o sekkyou shita tokoro de, (___).
items.en: Whatever I lecture my rebellious-phase son about, he simply won't listen.
items.hi: विद्रोही उम्र वाले बेटे को कुछ भी समझा लो, वह सुनने को तैयार ही नहीं।
items.gu: બળવાખોર ઉંમરના દીકરાને ગમે તે સમજાવો, તે સાંભળવા તૈયાર જ નથી.

opts.t: どうしたらいいでしょうか

items.why: c) says the lecturing is useless — the core meaning (無意味だ・無駄だ). a) says it would make things worse, which is a different idea from "pointless". b) is a question, not a negative judgment.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: こんなに給料が安くては、どんなに働いたところで、お金は（ ）。
items.qr: Konna ni kyuuryou ga yasukute wa, donna ni hataraita tokoro de, okane wa (___).
items.en: With pay this low, no matter how hard I work, I can't save any money.
items.hi: इतनी कम तनख़्वाह में, कितना भी काम कर लूँ, पैसे जमा नहीं होते।
items.gu: આટલા ઓછા પગારમાં, ગમે તેટલું કામ કરું, પૈસા બચતા નથી.
items.why: The ⚠ note: past sentences (過去の文) don't follow 〜たところで — it is a judgment about a hypothetical. a) is a present negative judgment. b) and c) are both past tense.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 財産があれば（ ）、面倒なこともある。
items.qr: Zaisan ga areba (___), mendou na koto mo aru.
items.en: Having a fortune brings its own headaches, too.
items.hi: धन-दौलत है तो उसकी भी अपनी झंझटें हैं।
items.gu: મિલકત હોય તો તેની પણ પોતાની ઝંઝટો હોય છે.

opts.en: (if you have it), then having it

items.why: The 🔗 line: 動 ば形 + 動 た形 + で → あればあったで. a) switches to the negative, breaking the "same word" rule. b) is the て形, not た形 + で.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 大学に合格したら（ ）入学金と学費の心配をしなければならない。
items.qr: Daigaku ni goukaku shitara (___) nyuugakukin to gakuhi no shinpai o shinakereba naranai.
items.en: Even once you've passed the university entrance exam, you then have to worry about the admission fee and tuition.
items.hi: विश्वविद्यालय में पास हो गए तो हो गए, फिर दाख़िला-शुल्क और फ़ीस की चिंता करनी पड़ती है।
items.gu: યુનિવર્સિટીમાં પાસ થયા તો થયા, પછી પ્રવેશ-ફી અને ફીની ચિંતા કરવી પડે છે.
items.why: 〜たら + た形 + で: 合格したら(合格)したで. a) uses the dictionary form, which isn't on the 🔗 line. c) したので ("because I passed") is a reason clause, not the repetition pattern, and it would not convey "a new problem appears".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 料理が余ったら余ったで、（ ）。
items.qr: Ryouri ga amattara amatta de, (___).
items.en: If there's food left over, that's fine — I'll eat it later, so don't worry about it.
items.hi: खाना बच गया तो बच गया, मैं बाद में खा लूँगा, आप चिंता मत कीजिए।
items.gu: જમવાનું વધ્યું તો વધ્યું, હું પછી ખાઈ લઈશ, તમે ચિંતા ન કરશો.

opts.t: どうしたらいいでしょうね
opts.en: what shall we do, I wonder?

opts.t: 後で食べますから気にしないでください
opts.r: ato de tabemasu kara ki ni shinaide kudasai
opts.en: I'll eat it later, so don't worry
opts.hi: मैं बाद में खा लूँगा, चिंता मत कीजिए
opts.gu: હું પછી ખાઈ લઈશ, ચિંતા ન કરશો

opts.t: 捨ててしまったほうがいいです
opts.r: sutete shimatta hou ga ii desu
opts.en: it's better to throw it out

items.why: This is the book's ③ direction: a feared situation (leftovers) is no problem. b) says exactly that. a) treats it as a problem with no solution yet; c) is advice to throw it away — neither expresses "it's fine either way".
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 斉藤さんが来なかったら来なかったで、（ ）。
items.qr: Saitou-san ga konakattara konakatta de, (___).
items.en: If Mr. Saito doesn't come, so be it — the five of us will discuss it and reach a conclusion.
items.hi: सैतो जी नहीं आए तो नहीं आए, हम पाँचों मिलकर चर्चा करके फ़ैसला कर लेंगे।
items.gu: સાઇતોજી ન આવ્યા તો ન આવ્યા, અમે પાંચેય ભેગા મળીને ચર્ચા કરીને નિર્ણય લઈ લઈશું.

opts.t: しばらく待ってみましょう
この5人で話し合って結論を出しましょう
opts.r: kono gonin de hanashiatte ketsuron o dashimashou
opts.en: let's decide among the five of us
opts.hi: हम पाँच मिलकर फ़ैसला कर लें

items.why: "He doesn't come → no problem, we carry on without him" — c). a) and b) still depend on him coming (calling, waiting), so they treat his absence as a problem to fix rather than accepting it.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 今さら（ ）、もう遅い。
items.qr: Imasara (___), mou osoi.
items.en: It's no use regretting it now — it's too late.
items.hi: अब पछताने से क्या फ़ायदा, अब बहुत देर हो चुकी है।
items.gu: હવે પસ્તાવાથી શું ફાયદો, હવે બહુ મોડું થઈ ગયું છે.

opts.t: 後悔しようがするまいが
opts.r: koukai shiyou ga suru mai ga
opts.en: whether you regret it or not

items.why: 今さら + "it's pointless" (もう遅い) is the textbook 〜たところで pattern. b) 〜ば〜たで needs "a new problem / no problem" after it. c) "whether or not" doesn't fit 今さら, which singles out the act of regretting as useless.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 彼は相手が（ ）、敬語を使わない。
items.qr: Kare wa aite ga (___), keigo o tsukawanai.
items.en: He doesn't use polite language, no matter who he's talking to.
items.hi: सामने चाहे कोई भी हो, वह आदरसूचक भाषा का प्रयोग नहीं करता।
items.gu: સામે ગમે તે હોય, તે આદરસૂચક ભાષા વાપરતો નથી.

opts.t: だれであろうとあるまいと
opts.r: dare de arou to aru mai to

opts.t: だれであったところで
opts.hi: कोई भी होता, तो भी बेकार
opts.gu: ગમે તે હોત, તો પણ નકામું

items.why: 疑問詞 + であれ = "whoever / whatever", and the result (no keigo) is unaffected → だれであれ. b) 〜うと〜まいと is "whether X or not X", which can't combine with a question word (だれ…or not?). c) たところで needs the result to be a negative judgment that the effort is pointless; "he doesn't use keigo" is a description of his habit.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: たとえ（ ）、判断ミスには謝罪するべきだ。
items.qr: Tatoe (___), handan misu ni wa shazai suru beki da.
items.en: Even if you're the company president, you should apologise for an error of judgment.
items.hi: चाहे कंपनी का अध्यक्ष ही क्यों न हो, ग़लत फ़ैसले के लिए माफ़ी माँगनी चाहिए।
items.gu: ભલે કંપનીના પ્રમુખ જ કેમ ન હોય, ખોટા નિર્ણય બદલ માફી માગવી જોઈએ.

opts.t: 社長だったら社長だったで
opts.en: if he's president, then being president…

opts.hi: चाहे अध्यक्ष ही क्यों न हो
opts.gu: ભલે પ્રમુખ જ કેમ ન હોય

items.why: たとえ + an extreme case (the president) + an obligation unaffected by it (謝罪するべきだ) = 〜であろうとも (【1】, noun form). a) 〜たら〜たで doesn't take たとえ and needs "a new problem / no problem". b) たところで can't be followed by an obligation like 〜べきだ (it needs a judgment that something is pointless).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 10課 · 逆接条件

items.q: 中学校の同窓会に（ ）べく、わたしはふるさとに帰った。
items.qr: Chuugakkou no dousoukai ni (___) beku, watashi wa furusato ni kaetta.
items.en: I went back to my hometown in order to attend my junior-high-school reunion.
items.hi: मिडिल स्कूल के पुराने सहपाठियों के मिलन-समारोह में भाग लेने के लिए मैं अपने गृहनगर लौटा।
items.gu: માધ્યમિક શાળાના જૂના સહપાઠીઓના મિલન-સમારંભમાં ભાગ લેવા માટે હું મારા વતન પાછો ગયો.
items.why: べく takes the dictionary form (する-verbs: するべく or すべく). a) the ます-stem is not a permitted connection (×参加しべく). c) 〜たい is an adjective of desire, not a volitional verb — べく already contains the "intending to" meaning.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: アルバイトを始めるべく、（ ）。
items.qr: Arubaito o hajimeru beku, (___).
items.en: In order to start a part-time job, he got the necessary documents together.
items.hi: पार्ट-टाइम नौकरी शुरू करने के लिए उसने ज़रूरी काग़ज़ात इकट्ठे किए।
items.gu: પાર્ટ-ટાઇમ નોકરી શરૂ કરવા માટે તેણે જરૂરી કાગળો ભેગા કર્યા.

opts.t: 彼は必要な書類をそろえた
opts.r: kare wa hitsuyou na shorui o soroeta

opts.t: 必要な書類がそろった
必要な書類は何ですか
opts.r: hitsuyou na shorui wa nan desu ka

items.why: The second clause must be a volitional action by the same subject — a) 彼は…そろえた (transitive, deliberate). b) uses the intransitive そろう: the documents are the subject and nobody acts. c) is a question to the listener (働きかけ), which the book bans after べく.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: これを田中さんに知らせるべく、メールを（ ）。
items.qr: Kore o Tanaka-san ni shiraseru beku, meeru o (___).
items.en: I wrote an email in order to let Mr. Tanaka know about this.
items.hi: यह बात तनाका जी को बताने के लिए मैंने ईमेल लिखा।
items.gu: આ વાત તનાકાજીને જણાવવા માટે મેં ઈમેલ લખ્યો.

opts.t: 書いておいてください
書いたほうがいいです

items.why: a) is the speaker's own deliberate action — fine. b) is a request and c) is advice; both are 働きかけ aimed at the listener, and they also break the same-subject rule (I intend → you write).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 小林氏は今度の選挙に立候補するべく、（ ）。
items.qr: Kobayashi-shi wa kondo no senkyo ni rikkouho suru beku, (___).
items.en: Mr. Kobayashi completed the paperwork in order to stand as a candidate in the coming election.
items.hi: कोबायाशी जी ने आगामी चुनाव में उम्मीदवार बनने के लिए सारी औपचारिकताएँ पूरी कर लीं।
items.gu: કોબાયાશીજીએ આગામી ચૂંટણીમાં ઉમેદવાર બનવા માટે બધી ઔપચારિકતાઓ પૂરી કરી લીધી.

opts.t: 党の応援が必要だった
opts.r: tou no ouen ga hitsuyou datta
opts.hi: पार्टी के समर्थन की ज़रूरत थी

items.why: Same subject (小林氏) + volitional action → b). a) switches the subject to 党 (the party). c) is a state (必要だった), not an action anyone takes.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: わが子の無罪を（ ）がため、母親は必死で証拠を探した。
items.qr: Wagako no muzai o (___) ga tame, hahaoya wa hisshi de shouko o sagashita.
items.en: Determined to prove her child's innocence, the mother searched desperately for evidence.
items.hi: अपने बच्चे की बेगुनाही साबित करने के लिए माँ ने जी-जान से सबूत ढूँढ़े।
items.gu: પોતાના બાળકની નિર્દોષતા સાબિત કરવા માટે માએ જીવ પર આવીને પુરાવા શોધ્યા.
items.why: The blank is followed by がため, so it needs the ん-form: する → せんがため. b) 証明するがため is not the pattern (the dictionary form goes with べく, not がため). c) the modern volitional しよう can't be glued to がため.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 戦争反対という思いを示さんがために、（ ）。
items.qr: Sensou hantai to iu omoi o shimesa n ga tame ni, (___).
items.en: Determined to show his opposition to war, he tried every possible method.
items.hi: युद्ध के विरोध की अपनी भावना दिखाने के लिए उसने हर संभव तरीक़ा आज़माया।
items.gu: યુદ્ધના વિરોધની પોતાની લાગણી બતાવવા માટે તેણે દરેક શક્ય રીત અજમાવી.

opts.t: どんな方法があるのか
opts.r: donna houhou ga aru no ka

opts.t: さまざまな方法がある
彼はあらゆる方法を試みた
opts.r: kare wa arayuru houhou o kokoromita

items.why: After 〜んがために comes a deliberate action by the person who has the purpose → c). a) is a question and b) a statement of existence (ある) — neither is anyone's purposeful act.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 権力を保たんがために、彼は（ ）。
items.qr: Kenryoku o tamota n ga tame ni, kare wa (___).
items.en: Determined to hold on to power, he resorted to forceful measures.
items.hi: सत्ता बनाए रखने के लिए उसने सख़्त क़दम उठाए।
items.gu: સત્તા ટકાવી રાખવા માટે તેણે કડક પગલાં લીધાં.
items.why: a) is a volitional action taken for the purpose. b) is a state (実力がある), and c) is a (failed) potential form — neither is something done "in order to" keep power.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 当選者には5日以内に賞品をお送りします。（ ）をもって当選発表といたします。
items.qr: Tousensha ni wa itsuka inai ni shouhin o o-okuri shimasu. (___) o motte tousen happyou to itashimasu.
items.en: Winners will be sent their prize within five days. The dispatch of the prize will serve as the announcement of the winners.
items.hi: विजेताओं को 5 दिनों के भीतर पुरस्कार भेजा जाएगा। पुरस्कार का भेजा जाना ही विजेता-घोषणा माना जाएगा।
items.gu: વિજેતાઓને 5 દિવસની અંદર ઇનામ મોકલવામાં આવશે. ઇનામ મોકલવું એ જ વિજેતા-જાહેરાત ગણાશે.
items.why: The formal notice says what act stands in for the announcement: 賞品の発送 (the sending). a) 宅配便 is an everyday, concrete delivery method — exactly what the ⚠ note says 〜をもって is not used for. c) the prize itself is an object, not a means of announcing anything.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 森田さんは（ ）をもって病気を克服したのである。
items.qr: Morita-san wa (___) o motte byouki o kokufuku shita no de aru.
items.en: It was through effort far greater than anyone else's that Mr. Morita overcame his illness.
items.hi: मोरिता जी ने दूसरों से कहीं ज़्यादा मेहनत के बल पर बीमारी पर जीत पाई थी।
items.gu: મોરિતાજીએ બીજાઓ કરતાં અનેકગણી મહેનતના બળે બીમારી પર જીત મેળવી હતી.
items.why: 〜をもって wants an abstract, admirable means — 人一倍の努力 fits the praising tone of 〜のである. b) a medicine and c) meals are concrete, everyday things you simply use; the book says 〜をもって is not used for 日常的・具体的な道具や方法 (you'd say 薬で／食事で).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 彼の実力をもってすれば、（ ）。
items.qr: Kare no jitsuryoku o motte sureba, (___).
items.en: With his ability, success is surely guaranteed.
items.hi: उसकी क़ाबिलियत के बल पर, सफलता पक्की है।
items.gu: તેની ક્ષમતાના બળે, સફળતા નક્કી છે.

opts.t: 今大会での優勝は無理だろう
opts.r: kon taikai de no yuushou wa muri darou
opts.en: winning this tournament is probably impossible
opts.hi: इस प्रतियोगिता में जीतना शायद नामुमकिन है
opts.gu: આ સ્પર્ધામાં જીતવું કદાચ અશક્ય છે

opts.t: 成功は間違いないだろう

opts.hi: फिर भी चिंता बनी रहती है

items.why: 〜をもってすれば is the fixed phrase that praises the power of ~, so the conclusion must be positive → b). a) and c) are negative/doubtful conclusions that contradict that praise.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: だれもがこのイベントに（ ）、配慮がなされている。
items.qr: Dare mo ga kono ibento ni (___), hairyo ga nasarete iru.
items.en: Care has been taken so that anyone can take part in this event.
items.hi: इस बात का ध्यान रखा गया है कि कोई भी इस कार्यक्रम में भाग ले सके।
items.gu: એ વાતનું ધ્યાન રાખવામાં આવ્યું છે કે કોઈ પણ આ કાર્યક્રમમાં ભાગ લઈ શકે.

opts.en: (×) in order to be able to take part
(×) determined to be able to take part

items.why: 参加できる is a potential (non-volitional) verb, and the subjects differ (だれも vs. the organisers who 配慮する). 〜べく and 〜んがため both need a volitional verb and the same subject, so a) and b) fail. 〜ように is the normal "so that" for potential verbs and different subjects.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: この雑誌には（ ）誇張表現が多いようだ。
items.qr: Kono zasshi ni wa (___) kochou hyougen ga ooi you da.
items.en: This magazine seems full of exaggerated expressions meant purely to sell copies.
items.hi: लगता है इस पत्रिका में सिर्फ़ बिक्री बढ़ाने के लिए की गई बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर बातें बहुत हैं।
items.gu: લાગે છે કે આ સામયિકમાં માત્ર વેચાણ વધારવા માટે કરેલી અતિશયોક્તિ ઘણી છે.
items.why: The blank modifies a noun (誇張表現). 〜んがため can do that as 〜んがための + N (book example ③ 得んがための発言), and it carries the critical "just to sell" tone. b) ×べくの does not exist. c) べく links clauses, so it can't sit directly before a noun.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: （ ）卒業の試験の代わりとします。
items.qr: (___) sotsugyou no shiken no kawari to shimasu.
items.en: Submission of a thesis will take the place of the graduation exam.
items.hi: शोध-प्रबंध जमा करना ही स्नातक परीक्षा के बदले माना जाएगा।
items.gu: મહાનિબંધ જમા કરાવવો એ જ સ્નાતક પરીક્ષાના બદલે ગણાશે.

opts.t: 論文を提出せんがため
opts.r: ronbun o teishutsu sen ga tame

opts.en: in order to submit a thesis

items.why: The sentence is an official rule saying what serves as the exam — a means, not a purpose → 〜をもって (+ 〜とする, typical notice style). a) and b) are purpose forms: "in order to submit a thesis, we'll treat it as the exam" makes no sense.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 11課 · 目的・手段

items.q: 内容が高度（ ）こそ、わかりやすく説明する必要がある。
items.qr: Naiyou ga koudo (___) koso, wakariyasuku setsumei suru hitsuyou ga aru.
items.en: It's precisely because the content is advanced that it needs to be explained clearly.
items.hi: विषय-वस्तु ऊँचे स्तर की है, इसीलिए उसे आसान ढंग से समझाना ज़रूरी है।
items.gu: વિષયવસ્તુ ઊંચા સ્તરની છે, એટલે જ તેને સરળ રીતે સમજાવવી જરૂરી છે.
items.why: The 🔗 line gives な-adjectives/nouns the shape −であればこそ. a) and c) build on たら, which ばこそ never uses (and たらば is an archaic hypothetical — the opposite of the factual reason ばこそ expresses).
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 12課 · 原因・理由

items.q: 忙しければこそ、（ ）のだ。
items.qr: Isogashikereba koso, (___) no da.
items.en: It's precisely because you're busy that you get good at using your time.
items.hi: व्यस्त हो, इसीलिए तो समय का इस्तेमाल अच्छे से करना आ जाता है।
items.gu: વ્યસ્ત હો, એટલે જ તો સમયનો ઉપયોગ સારી રીતે કરતાં આવડી જાય છે.

opts.t: ご飯を食べる時間もない
opts.r: gohan o taberu jikan mo nai
opts.en: there's not even time to eat
opts.hi: खाना खाने का भी समय नहीं

opts.t: 時間の使い方がうまくなる
opts.r: jikan no tsukaikata ga umaku naru
opts.hi: समय का सही इस्तेमाल करना आ जाता है
opts.gu: સમયનો સારો ઉપયોગ કરતાં આવડે છે

items.why: ばこそ highlights a reason you wouldn't normally expect — busyness leading to better time management (c) is that kind of twist. a) and b) are the obvious, direct consequences of being busy; for those a plain から／ので is enough.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 12課 · 原因・理由

items.q: 収入が少なければこそ、（ ）のだ。
items.qr: Shuunyuu ga sukunakereba koso, (___) no da.
items.en: It's precisely because our income is small that we make the effort to live happily.
items.hi: आमदनी कम है, इसीलिए तो हम ख़ुशी से जीने की कोशिश करते हैं।
items.gu: આવક ઓછી છે, એટલે જ તો અમે ખુશીથી જીવવાનો પ્રયત્ન કરીએ છીએ.

opts.t: 楽しく暮らす努力をする
opts.en: (we) make an effort to live happily
opts.hi: ख़ुशी से जीने की कोशिश करते हैं

items.why: Same logic as Q2: the book's meaning line includes "〜からあえてそうする" (because of ~, one deliberately does so) — c) is that deliberate, unexpected response. a) and b) are the predictable negative results.
items.unit: 新完全マスター 第1部 12課 · 原因・理由

items.q: わたしたち二人の関係が良ければこそ、（ ）。
items.qr: Watashitachi futari no kankei ga yokereba koso, (___).
items.en: It's precisely because the two of us get along so well that we can say whatever we want freely, isn't it?
items.hi: हम दोनों के रिश्ते अच्छे हैं, इसीलिए तो हम जो चाहें खुलकर कह पाते हैं, है न?
